messages.content: Hi

hi, i’m tal

i help people find the best ‘next job’
i scan 50,000 roles a day to find the best 1 for you.

so… what’s your full name?
Bandla karthik
which company are you working at?
Cognizant
cognizant... and what's your role there?
DevSecOps engineer

interesting.

is this you? https://in.linkedin.com/in/karthik-bandla-95b701251
Yes that's me

karthik, your profile is playing it close to the chest.

looks like you've been too busy building things at cognizant to update it.

how long have you been in the game? total years working?
I'm a case graduate 2025 I started my internship at cognizant in February and my full time role from August 2025

got it. so you're just starting out.

what are you hoping to do in your first real role? what kind of work gets you excited?
I have 7 months experience in devsecops cybersecurity
and where? bangalore, remote, anywhere?
Hyderabad
I've got a sense for what you're looking for. Be back in less than a minute
i'm scanning through 50,000 jobs to find the perfect fit for you. you'll hear from me soon.
Predict Your Future

you're standing at a fork in the road.

path one: the cognizant comfort zone.
you'll learn process, see how big ships turn (slowly).
you'll be safe. but you'll feel the golden handcuffs clicking within two years.

path two: the specialist's leap.
you take the cognizant brand name, sharpen your devsecops skills for 18 months, and then you jump.
to a product company that's bleeding for your skills.

one path gives you comfort. the other gives you a legacy.
the choice is already being made.
I want legacy I'm preparing for dsa and system design

legacy it is.

dsa and system design are the entry ticket. everyone's grinding that.
but your legacy won't be in writing perfect sorting algorithms.

it'll be in building unbreachable fortresses.
focus on cloud-native security. kubernetes security, service mesh, infrastructure as code security.
that's the stuff that gets you the insane valuation multiples at product companies.

stop thinking like a developer.
start thinking like a defender.
What you want me to do now whether to become a developer or a security specialist

that's the wrong question.

developers are builders. security specialists are guards.
you need to be the architect.

the one who designs the fortress and also knows how to lay the bricks.
don't choose. combine.
How can I become an architect

you don't "become" an architect by taking a course.
it's a mindset.

at cognizant, for every project, ask one question:
"how can this entire system be compromised?"

not just your part. the whole thing.
trace the data flow. find the weak points. where are the blind spots?

then go home and build a side project that solves a real-world security problem you found at work.
not a to-do list app. a real solution.

architects aren't given the title.
they just start doing the job.
